pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:1295 The OAuth gateway behind oauthGatewayApi.ts takes an oidcIssuer from the webview and fetches its discovery document through SHARED_HTTP, which has no SSRF-safe resolver and follows redirects by default; the token_endpoint the discovery document returns gets only a string host-suffix check before the client_secret and auth code are POSTed to it through the same client, even though the repo already ships SSRF_SAFE_HTTP for exactly this case.

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/oauth.rs:1205 validate_issuer_url judges only an IP literal in the string, never the resolved address. IPv6 private and unique-local ranges are not covered, the verdict is not bound to the connection, redirects are not re-judged, and the custom authorize_url/token_url branch (oauth.rs:2073) is not validated at all before the secret is sent.
src/api/vault/rotation.ts:53 The UI-driven refresh sends only a credential id and the backend loads and attaches the token. The raw-refresh-token IPC door was retired (oauthGatewayApi.ts:65-72).
src/lib/bindings/OAuthStatusResult.ts:17 The poll contract has no token field at all, only booleans plus an opaque session ref, so no token value can reach the webview.

src-tauri/src/commands/credentials/crud.rs:69 The OAuth result the renderer brings back is an opaque id into a server-side session table and is redeemed server-side. This is the 'keep it server-side' arm of the technique.

pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/cloud/sync/rows.rs:3 The sync writer is a deliberate regime-one client: it holds only the public anon key plus the user's JWT, its projections structurally never select vault or encrypted columns, and it omits user_id so the store defaults the owner from auth.uid().

techniques.evidence: src-tauri/src/cloud/sync/client.rs:5 Only SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_ANON_KEY are compiled in, and the code states they are public by design. No service-role key exists in app code; the service_role hits are user connector fields.

src-tauri/src/cloud/sync/rows.rs:11 Vault tables, per-device ciphertext columns and payload_iv are excluded by shape. Residual: the persona_events payload is value-filtered by a denylist scrubber (key_is_secret plus token prefixes), not omitted.

src-tauri/src/cloud/sync/rows.rs:14 The owner is defaulted from auth.uid() and deliberately omitted with a comment saying why, and a test enforces it (rows_never_send_user_id). The policy DDL lives in another repo, so the policy-coverage half was not verifiable here.
src-tauri/src/cloud/sync/client.rs:22 The destination is fixed by the deployment, which is the technique's own exclusion.
src-tauri/src/cloud/sync/client.rs:3 This is regime one by design: there is no privileged upstream to broker.

pairs.subject: browser-credential-boundary
pairs.evidence: src-tauri/src/mcp_bin.rs:102 personas-mcp is a stdio JSON-RPC sidecar with no browser client, no listening socket, no bundled public key and no web storage; a search of src-tauri/src/mcp_server for anon_key, VITE_, TcpListener and localStorage found none. Its vault reads go out as an outbound client to the app's loopback credential proxy (tools.rs bridge_proxy), so the boundary it touches is owned by the management API's context, not this one.
